Latest News
Well done year 5 for completing another week!
In English this week, we have completed writing our final draft of a newspaper article includingindirect/direct speech and subordinating conjunctions. We have now looked at a WAGOLL of anon – chronological report about Ancient Egypt. We have also learnt one of our key skillsrelative clauses. Next week we will learn about parenthesis and how to use it!
In Maths, we have now finished our place value topic. The children have also done their end ofblock assessment for this. We have now started our addition and subtraction topic. They havelearnt how to use mental strategies and add whole numbers with more than four digits.
In science, we learnt about air resistance, and we did a little experiment to understand how airresistance can change depending on size, mass and surface area.
In History, we learned about the process of mumification. The children created a lovelyposter/leaflet to showcase their understanding of this process.
In Shared reading, we have carried on reading Beowulf and started our next chapter. Thechildren have worked on their inference skills, retrieval skills and even practiced some SATSstyle assessment questions.
We also celebrated languages day this afternoon. We were given Lithuania! We practiced somewords from the language and learnt about paper weaving. They created beautiful pieces.
The children have also been given a letter about a visit on November 17th 2026.
As always, ensure your child is reading and going on TTRS 5 x a week.
Reads are counted on Fridays.
Enjoy your weekends!

Well done for another great week everyone!
In Maths this week, we have been learning about rounding numbers to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000. We have focused on identifying the correct place value column to look at and remembering the rule that 5 or more means we round up.
We have also begun exploring Roman numerals and have started practising how to write the date using Roman numerals.
In English, we completed the final draft of our character description of Lila, from our class text The Firework-Maker’s Daughter.
We worked hard to make our writing interesting and descriptive by using; expanded noun phrases, similes, possessive apostrophes and subordinating conjunctions.
The children have shown great care in developing and improving their writing.
On Friday, we celebrated European Day of Languages. Our chosen country was Spain, and we focused on Spanish art and the work of the famous architect and artist Antoni Gaudi.
The pupils explored Gaudi’s distinctive style and then created their own Gaudi-inspired artwork. We were very impressed with the creativity and imagination shown in their designs.
Well done to everyone for another fantastic week of learning!
This week in Reception we have been focusing on the story The Rainbow Fish! We have discussed what it means to be kind, to share and to speak about friendships. We decorated our own Rainbow fish by selecting a range of materials, the pupils really enjoyed creating their own patterns and designs.
In maths, we have been focusing on forming numerals 1-5 and sorting objects in different ways. We have also been looking at our fine motor skills, by practising using scissors and holding our pencils withthe correct tripod grip.
Your children have also started to bring home a library book! We visit and change our library books every Monday. Please ensure you are reading with your child atleast 3 times a week. Each time you read with your child, please write it in their reading records so they can be rewarded for their hard work!

This week we have been focusing on 'Me and My Emotions'. The children have been practising coping strategies for when feelings of frustration or anger arise by 'smelling the flowers, blowing out the candles'. They have been talking about different emotions and how they might feel at different times throughout the day. Next week our focus story will be 'Giraffes Can't Dance'.
Well done Year 1! You have had another fantastic week of learning and have worked incredibly hard across all of our subjects!
In English, we designed our very own gingerbread men and carefully labelled their different features. We then used our designs to help us write sentences about our gingerbread men.
In Maths, we have been learning about greater than and less than, comparing different numbers and using our mathematical knowledge to decide which number is greater or smaller.
In Science, we explored sense of taste by trying a variety of different foods. We discussed whether they tasted sweet, salty or sour and ranked the different foods based on their taste.
We also had a very exciting trip to Barleylands, where we made our own gingerbread men, met and stroked different animals, and even had the oppurtunity to feed some of them! The children had a wonderful time and represnted Year 1 brilliantly.
Finally, we celebrated Europen day of Languages! Year 1 explored Finland, learning a little bit about the country and creating beautiful Nothern Lights silhouette art work inspired by Finlands night skies.
Well done Year 1 for another lovely week. Have a lovely weekend!
20260922_1123521.jpg
It has been another wonderful week in Year 6, with the children continuing to show enthusiasm, resilience and a fantastic attitude towards their learning.
In English, we have begun our next writing unit, working towards a character description based on our class text, Street Child. Throughout the week, the children have explored how authors bring characters to life through the use of expanded noun phrases and relative clauses. They have enjoyed investigating the character of Grimy Nick and thinking carefully about how to create vivid descriptions that capture both appearance and personality. We are excited to see the children put all of these skills into practice when they complete their final pieces next week.
In Maths, we have moved on to our units of addition and subtraction, alongside multiplication and division. The children have been working incredibly hard to apply their knowledge, tackle challenges and explain their mathematical reasoning. We have been particularly impressed by their perseverance and positive attitude when faced with more complex problems.
In History, the children became historians as they carried out independent research into the Industrial Revolution. Using their findings, they created PowerPoint presentations and confidently shared their learning with their classmates. We were so proud of the effort, independence and presentation skills they demonstrated throughout the project. It was wonderful to see the children taking ownership of their learning and sharing their knowledge with such confidence.
In Science, we explored the fascinating structure of the human eye and learned more about how our brains process light to help us see the world around us. In Art, the children continued developing their abstract artwork, showing creativity, imagination and care as they refined their pieces.
This afternoon we also celebrated European languages day and year 6 learned all about Viking runes and created viking shields with messages on them displayed in the windows for you to see!
Thank you, as always, for your continued support. It has been lovely to see how hard the children are working and how much pride they are taking in their learning.
We hope you have a lovely weekend and look forward to another exciting week of learning ahead.
We have had a noisy and active week in Rainbow Room this week.
The core word focus was the word 'no'. We completed mark making using a variety of tools and enjoyed some music based around the word 'no'. Phonics sounds were e, l, h and sh.
In maths, the pupils have enjoyed the focus on 10 Green Bottles. We have been completing lots of individual maths activities to secure their concrete knowledge. We will be continuing with this over the forthcoming weeks.
The sensory activities have been nice and messy allowing us to introduce and use lots of useful vocabulary. Jelly using the words 'cold', 'wet' and 'slimy' as well as pushing cars through different materials and saying 'push'.
Today was languages day and we all made Venetian masks using our gluing skills. Make sure you take a look at our masks in the Rainbow Room window!

Art & DT
The Art and Design Technology curriculum aims to foster creativity, build upon critical thinking and practical skill development in pupils. Artistic expression and design thinking are essential components of a well-rounded education. Our Art and DT curriculum provides pupils with opportunities to develop and extend their knowledge and skills and to be able to express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas. Over time, pupils will develop their knowledge and skills withina range of medias such as drawing, painting, printing, collage, textiles and sculpture.
At Brady, we use Cornerstones Education to outline our Art & DT curriculum.

Computing
At Brady we follow the Teach Computing scheme of work. This scheme of learning has been written to support all pupils. Each lesson is sequenced so that it builds on the learning from the previous lesson, and where appropriate, activities are scaffolded so that all pupils can succeed and thrive. Scaffolded activities provide pupils with extra resources, such asvisual prompts, to reach the same learning goals as the rest of the class. Exploratory tasks foster a deeper understanding of a concept, encouraging pupils to apply their learning in different contexts and make connections with other learning experiences.

English
Reading at Brady is taught through Read Write Inc. from EYFS to the end of Key Stage 1. From the end of Year 2, children become familiar with our comprehension skills aka the VIPERs. In Key Stage 2, the children begin Shared Reading lessons. In these lessons chapter books are read, discussed and comprehension skills are taught whilst exploring these texts. They also learn about the VIPERs reading skills in more depth and complete comprehension activities around these each week. All the texts that children read, whether in their English lessons, as part of shared reading, or end of the day story books, are chosen carefully to ensure the pupils at Brady are exposed to great authors, diverse texts and authors, books relating to their topics and books that just inspire and engage!
Click here to see our Curriculum policy - Reading
Take a look at some of the amazing books your child will have enjoyed by the time they finish their journey at Brady with us!
At Brady, we believe the best writing comes from being inspired and engaged. This is why teachers carefully plan sequenced lessons around a core text (usually the same as the shared reading text in Key Stage 2), real life experiences or cross curriculuar topics that have captured the imagination of the pupils.
In EYFS and Key Stage 1, teachers embed the necessary skills the children need to become competent writers. Lessons are based around engaging core texts and give pupils the opportunity to practise their transcription, spelling, grammar and handwriting skills. In these Key Stages, teachers work hard to reduce the cognitive load by using familiar sequences of learning and focus on skill mastery before explicitly teaching many genres of writing.
In Key Stage 2, the teachers follow the 'writing journey' when planning their writing lessons. This enables children to be exposed to different genres of writing, whilst practising new grammar skills and having the opportunity to use these skills in context.
Poetry is also taught throughout Key Stage 1 to Key Stage 2. These units follow a progression, ensuring the pupils are exposed to and have experience of writing a range of genres of poetry during their time at Brady.
Click here to see our Curriculum policy - Writing

Welcome to

Languages - French
At Brady we use the Language Angels scheme of work and resources to ensure we offer a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious foreign languages curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes. All pupils will be expected to achieve their full potential by encouraging high expectations and excellent standards in their foreign language learning - the ultimate aim being that pupils will feel willing and able to continue studying languages beyond key stage 2.
The curriculum will be updated and reviewed annually, creating a dynamic programme of study that will be clearly outlined in both long-term and short-term planning. This will ensure that the foreign language knowledge of our pupils progresses within each academic year and is extended year upon year throughout the primary phase and, in so doing, will always be relevant and in line with meeting or exceeding national DfE requirements.
The four key language learning skills; listening, speaking, reading and writing will be taught and all necessary grammar will be covered in an age-appropriate way across the primary phase. This will enable pupils to use and apply their learning in a variety of contexts, laying down solid foundations for future language learning and also helping the children improve overall attainment in other subject areas.
Throughout the year, pupils have also had the opportunity to take part in languages after school clubs. More details can be found here.

Maths
The language of mathematics is international. The basic skills of mathematics are vital for the life opportunities of our children. Our aim is for all children to think mathematically, enabling them to reason, solve problems and assess risk in a range of contexts.At Brady Primary School our curated mastery approach has been developed to ensure every child can achieve excellence in mathematics. Children can experience a sense of pride and achievement as they solve a problem for the first time, discover different solutions and make links between different areas of mathematics. It provides pupils with a deep understanding of the subject through a concrete, pictorial and abstract approach. This ensures pupils fully understand what they are learning.We understand the significance that a fun, deep and broad mathematics education can have on outcomes for children both now and in their future. Like many other schools we follow the White Rose Maths Scheme of Learning (SoL) which has been developed by experts to build mathematical understanding through the principles of a ‘concrete, pictorial, abstract’ approach. We firmly believe that all children should have access to varied fluency, reasoning and problem-solving challenges in every teaching sequence.

PSHE / Relationships and Health Education
At Brady we use 1Decision to teach our PSHE curriculum including Relationships and Health education. This scheme includes an updated curriculum that meets new Department for Education statutory guidance as of 1 September 2026.
DfE: Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education September 2026
The 1Decision scheme of learning is a comprehensive programme which gives pupils a broad and in-depth Personal, Social, Health, and Economic (PSHE) education. The programme includes a series of age appropriate interactive videos with alternative endings, giving every pupil the opportunity to explore different choices and understand the consequences of their decisions through powerful social story experiences.
The modules cover a wide range of essential topics that support personal development, embed British Values, and promote an understanding of protected characteristics. They also equip pupils with the knowledge and skills they need to stay safe, stay healthy, build positive relationships, navigate online risks, and much more.
Importantly, all of our resources are created to remain respectful of different family traditions, cultural backgrounds, and beliefs, ensuring that every child feels included, represented, and supported in their learning journey.
Click here to find out more information about 1Decision on the parent/carer zone
PSHE, RSHE & Drugs Policy September 2026

Science
At Brady Primary we believe that acquiring scientific skills and knowledge is the key to children’s understanding of the natural and technological world around them. Children’s natural curiosity will be utilised in developing the necessary skills of inquiry and questioning which are needed to become effective scientists and to begin to develop a responsible attitude towards the environment.
We involve problem solving opportunities that allow children to find out for themselves. Children are encouraged to ask their own questions and be given opportunities to use their scientific skills and research to discover the answers.We build upon the learning and skill development of the previous years.
We aim for Science at Brady to result in a fun, engaging, high-quality science education, that provides children with the foundations and knowledge for understanding the world. Children learn the possibilities for careers in science, as a result of Science Days, ensuring that children have an understanding and exposure to a range of different scientists from various backgrounds, all children feel they are scientists and capable of achieving. We aim to ensure every child enjoys science which results in motivated learners with sound scientific understanding.

Wrap Around Care
Wraparound Care at Brady Primary School provided by Holloway Coaching
Holloway Coaching is proud to provide the Wraparound Care provision at Brady Primary School, offering a safe, welcoming and enjoyable environment for children before and after the school day.
Our experienced team provides a varied programme designed to keep children active, engaged and happy, while also giving them the opportunity to relax and socialise with their friends.
Children attending our Wraparound Care can enjoy a range of activities, including:
· Sports and team games
· Board games and puzzles
· Creative activities
· Indoor and outdoor play
· Quiet and relaxation time
· A variety of fun, child-led activities
Parents and carers can book Breakfast Club and After School Club sessions directly through the Holloway Coaching online booking system, Holloway Coaching accept Tax-Free Child-Care payments through Poncho Pay on our booking system Pebble.
We recommend booking sessions as early as possible to secure your child's place and to help us plan appropriate staffing for each session.
